about: Points marked by hand: read by eye off crops of the original input, each a crop of the stated box (left, top, right, bottom, in the original's pixels) enlarged `zoom` times with a 10 px grid labelled in the original's pixels. Pixel coordinates are the original's, with (0, 0) the top left corner of the top left pixel's centre. Nothing here is moved after a fit; spike.py records what it does to each mark.

rowsAcross.note: the row of round pads behind the long pads at the front edge
the row of round pads behind the long pads at the front edge
the row of round pads behind the long pads at the front edge

frame.what: Task 2: the first and last pad of every connector row on the 0.1 inch pitch that runs across the board (x) with at least eight pads, marked on I1 for the board's x scale. The rule was set before any of them was fitted: every such row, and the rows of the DIPs that lie across (IC74 and IC75, from the scale section), and nothing else; the rear sockets (SK1 to SK7) are on their own pitches (SK6, a D socket, is on 2.77 mm) and are not used. The pitch count is the pads counted on a 1:2 view of each connector with a 20 px grid, and agrees with the row's length in pixels at 2.54 mm. board_frame.py moves each mark to the centroid of the solder blob nearest it (common.refine_to_pad), refusing a move over 0.6 mm, and finds every pad between them the same way.

excluded.why: In O1 the space bar is seen almost edge on, and its top face cannot be told from its front face; excluded before any fit

repeat.what: Both corners read a second time on wider crops, after the first reading gave a STOP, to check the marks; not used for the figure judged

frontEdge.what: The two front corners of the case's top as O1 shows them: where the line of the side meets the line of the front, the corners being rounded

repeats.what: Five keys marked a second time on crops placed differently, to show how well a mark repeats. Not used in any fit.

keys.what: The centre of each keycap's top face (the dished face the legend is on), read as the middle of its outline left to right and between its rear edge and the highlight on its front edge. Not refined in code. `k1` is the switch in K1 under that key.

scale.folds: Set before any fit: the footprints alternate A, B, A, B in the order listed here. The scale is fitted on one half and scored on the other, both ways round, so every footprint is held out once.

footprints.note: The 28-pin footprint at the board's left edge, below R173; the label printed beside it was not read with confidence, so it is named by its place

scale.what: The centres of the four corner pins of each DIP footprint: pins 1, N/2, N/2 + 1 and N in some order, named by where they lie in the scan (tl, tr, bl, br: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right). Which corner is pin 1 does not matter to the scale. The pin count is the one a row's length in pixels allows at the 2.54 mm pitch (the next count up or down is 2.54 mm, about 40 px, away). spike.py moves each mark to the centroid of the solder blob nearest it (common.refine_to_pad), and refuses the move when that centroid is over 0.6 mm from the mark.

solderSeeds.what: Four pads marked on I1 and on I2 mirrored (I2 flipped left to right, x' = 5013 - x, so that it lies as the component side does), to seed the solder side's first affine fit. They are corners of four footprints far apart.

footprints.what: Footprints' references, read from I1's print by hand because nothing in board_register.py reads text: each mark is a point in I1 pixels inside the footprint it names, with the crop (I1 pixels, enlarged by zoom; a label on the side of a footprint is turned upright) the label was read on, and the reason. A mark with pin1 also names pin 1, for a footprint whose print chamfer the code could not find. A mark with pins says how many pins a DIP has where the grouping's run is longer than its printed outline, and keeps that many slots round the point. A mark with outlineFaint says the outline's print is too faint on one side for the grouping's outline test, which the stronger side then passes alone. A mark with kind says the grouping took something for a DIP that is not one. A mark with ref null and unread true says the reference is on the board and cannot be read; none is needed in this run, every DIP's was read. Every DIP footprint has a mark; the connectors PL8 to PL14 and SK6 and the resistor packs RP1 and RP2 are marked too, where the print is legible; no other connector or single row is.

i5Pins.what: Chip pins on I5 (8BS's photograph of a populated Issue 7 board, in its pixels as stored, 2048 by 1536, not turned by its EXIF orientation: stored that way it lies as I1 does, rear connectors at the top), for registering I5 to the board frame (task 4's "I5 to I1" check). Each is the centroid of a pin's leg where it shows as a bright blob (OKLab L over 0.75, chroma under 0.05, 8 to 150 pixels), the blob picked by eye on the crop as the leg of the named pin: the corner pins of 14 chips spread over the board, or the pin next to a corner whose leg is hidden. The candidates were proposed by a rough fit (an affine from eight chips' centres read by eye on a reduced copy, then a homography refitted on the candidates within 3 pixels) and each was checked on its crop; the chips whose legs were ambiguous on their crops (the packed RAM, IC20, IC53, IC56, IC68), in sockets (IC6) or empty (IC78) were left out. Marked on 13 October 2026, before the check was run. The leg is seen from above, so its centroid can sit up to about half a millimetre outside the pad's centre, away from the chip's body.

identities.what: Each IC's marking as read by hand on the crops board_parts.py --crops writes (each IC's body and 3 mm round it, drawn onto the board frame through the photograph's fit at 12 pixels a millimetre, enlarged twice, turned so its rows run across, in sheets of eight in out/, git-ignored); read on 13 October 2026, after the method was fixed. reading is every line read, in order, the maker's logo left out; null with why where nothing could be read. populated: the photograph shows a part in the place. socket: true where a socket shows clearly (an empty one, or a frame round the part); absent where none was seen, which does not mean there is none.
